patternLegend.focused-capability: Focused production capability with declared inputs and outputs, IaC support, least privilege, encryption, monitoring, alerting, rollback, disaster recovery, and production acceptance criteria.
patternLegend.provision-from-code: Provision from reviewed infrastructure code and pinned artifacts with security and cost guardrails, verified live endpoints, and a tested rollback or teardown path.
patternLegend.runbook-definition: Operating runbook definition with prerequisites, accountable roles, ordered actions, approval and rollback points, escalation paths, recovery objectives, required evidence, and a verified completion condition.
patternLegend.decision-matrix: Weighted decision procedure across availability, latency, residency, security, operational burden, recovery targets, scalability, lock-in, and total cost, with rejected options recorded.
patternLegend.evaluation-gate: Evaluation gate with explicit pass, warn, and fail thresholds; retains environment, region, resource identifiers, observed evidence, risk rating, owner, remediation, and a repeatable retest procedure.
patternLegend.operate-service: Operated through versioned configuration, least-privilege access, encryption, quotas, health checks, observability, automated recovery, and clearly tested failure behavior.

coreProductionAcceptance: Infrastructure plans are reviewed, policy-checked, and applied through versioned automation with remote encrypted state, locking, backups, and drift detection.
Production endpoints resolve through managed DNS, present valid TLS, withstand expected load, enforce WAF and rate-limit policies, and expose no unintended public services.
Applications, databases, queues, caches, storage, and secrets pass connectivity, authentication, encryption, backup, restoration, failover, and rollback tests.
Monitoring covers latency, traffic, errors, saturation, business health, logs, traces, uptime, certificate expiry, security events, and backup failures with tested alert delivery.
Recovery point and recovery time objectives are documented and proven through restoration and regional failover drills, not assumed from product marketing.
Production credentials are short-lived where possible, deployment and code-signing credentials are isolated, and emergency access is logged, reviewed, and regularly tested.
catalogDesignNotes: Keep provider-neutral control Skills separate from AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Cloudflare, and self-hosted implementation packs.
Prefer immutable artifacts and reviewed infrastructure code. Do not repair production by undocumented console changes.
Treat backup success as incomplete until the target data and full environment have been restored and validated against defined recovery objectives.
Separate monitoring from alerting. Collect useful signals first, then alert only on conditions that require timely human or automated action.
Make cost, security, privacy, reliability, and rollback requirements part of the deployment interface rather than post-launch cleanup.
